newsitem.title: USA: Man kills four in New Hampshire shooting spree.
newsitem.headline: Man kills four in New Hampshire shooting spree.

text.p: A man killed two state troopers, a judge and newspaper editor in the tiny New Hampshire town of Colebrook on Tuesday before fleeing into remote woods in neighboring Vermont, police said.

Police from two states were scouring the dense forest on foot and by helicopter for the man, described as "deranged and dangerous", after he escaped down logging trails in a police car and then fled on foot.

New Hampshire State Police identified the suspected killer as Carl Draga, 67, from Columbia, N.H. Residents in Colebrook, 20 miles (30 km) from the Canadian border, described Draga as militant and anti-government.
The shooting spree began when the man entered a local grocery store and killed two state troopers. He took their patrol car and drove to the local newspaper office.

"A man who everybody knows locally to be deranged and dangerous ... apparently caused some sort of commotion at LaPerle's (grocery store), shot two state troopers took their cruiser and went into town," News and Sentinel publisher John Harrigan said.

The gunman then killed lawyer Vickie Bunnell, who also served as an associate judge. Bunnell's office is in the same building as the newspaper, whose editor Dennis Jois died some hours after being shot, Harrigan told New Hampshire Public Radio.
A motive for the shootings remained unclear.
Colebrook is a community of 1,100 people located along the Connecticut river on the New Hampshire-Vermont border about 20 miles (30 km) south of Quebec.
New Hampshire police chased the suspect into Vermont's remote Northeast Kingdom region and Vermont state police said they were helping search for the man.
New Hampshire State Police Major David McCarthey told reporters the suspect abandoned the patrol car and continued on foot in a "very rural area."
